title: Starfall, a browser game built from scratch
brief: Please build a small browser game from scratch, in a folder called starfall inside the Projects folder in your home folder. In the game you steer a little ship along the bottom of the screen, dodge falling stars and catch energy orbs, and the stars fall faster as the score climbs. Use plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript only, all in that one folder, with no libraries and no internet. Do all the work in your own terminal, through the shell's agent_run action: that is how you make the folder, write each file and look at what you wrote. Do not use the Terminal app. Start by writing a short plan into a file called PLAN.md in that folder: a checklist of about eight steps, from an empty page to a finished game with a start screen, score, levels, keyboard and touch controls, and sound that stays off until the player turns it on. Then work through the plan one step at a time: write or change the files, then check the page by running `/opt/yantrik-live/director/check-page ~/Projects/starfall/index.html` through agent_run. It loads the game in a headless browser and prints any error the page throws; no output means it loaded clean. Fix every error it shows. Tick a step off in PLAN.md only when the code for it is really there and the check is clean: a tick is a promise to the people watching. People are watching the screen, so keep each step small and visible. When every step is ticked and the check is clean, say FINISHED on its own line.
keep_going: Please keep going on Starfall. Read PLAN.md in the starfall folder through the shell's agent_run action. If the folder or the plan does not exist yet, make them first, as the brief said. Otherwise take the first step that is not ticked, do it, and check the page by running `/opt/yantrik-live/director/check-page ~/Projects/starfall/index.html` through agent_run. Fix any error it prints, and tick the step off in PLAN.md only when its code is really there and the check is clean. If every step is ticked and the check is clean, say FINISHED on its own line.
